body_text: Meridianbet Extends EuroLeague Title Sponsorship with Red Star to 2030 admin 2025-12-30T13:32:34+00:00 Meridianbet, a leading sports betting and iGaming operator in 18 jurisdictions and a subsidiary of NASDAQ-listed Golden Matrix Group Inc. (NASDAQ: GMGI), has extended its title sponsorship deal with EuroLeague basketball club Crvena Zvezda (Red Star Belgrade) through 2030, maintaining one of European basketball’s most significant long-term private-sector partnerships. Meridianbet . Red Star 2030 The multi-year extension continues a relationship that began in January 2023, with the Serbian club competing under the name Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet across all competitions including EuroLeague, ABA League, and Serbian League. Meridianbet branding appears on team jerseys and throughout Belgrade Arena. 🏀 Meridianbet extends title sponsorship with @EuroLeague @kkcrvenazvezda through 2030. Nasdaq $GMGI continues multi-year investment in one of European basketball’s most significant partnerships. Full story on the first link. pic.twitter.com/yCw8w1rpeB — MeridianBet Group (@meridianbet_ofc) December 30, 2025 The deal reflects Meridianbet’s strategic focus on markets where basketball commands significant cultural relevance and media reach. Crvena Zvezda competes in the EuroLeague—a 20-team competition spanning 12 countries with a global fanbase exceeding 90 million—which serves as the primary European talent pipeline to the NBA. The club’s alumni include Hall of Famers Vlade Divac and Peja Stojakovic. “Extending our title sponsorship with Crvena Zvezda through 2030 reflects our commitment to long-term brand building in markets where basketball is more than a sport—it’s a way of life for fans, players, and entire communities,” said Zoran Milosevic, CEO of Meridianbet. “As we scale Meridianbet’s operations across 18 jurisdictions, partnerships with premier sports properties like Crvena Zvezda create sustained visibility with audiences that align with our customer demographics.” The partnership has delivered brand activation across Meridianbet’s core Balkan markets including Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro, while supporting dozens of CSR initiatives ranging from youth basketball development to responsible gaming education programs integrated into club communications.

title: How to Develop a Consistent Study Routine in 2026
summary: Learn how to develop a consistent study routine that works for you in 2026.
body_text: Keeping up with school can feel overwhelming when every week brings new assignments, readings, and deadlines. Many students share how hard it is to stay consistent and avoid falling into last minute studying, and it’s a pattern that feels familiar to anyone who has tried to balance a full course load. Building a steady study routine can make everything feel more manageable by giving your week structure and reducing the stress around daily tasks. With the right habits in place, studying becomes something you can approach with more confidence and less pressure. In this article, we'll outline how you can develop a consistent, effective study routine that actually works in 2026. Let's dive in! What is a Study Routine? A study routine is a structured plan that guides when, how, and where you study. It helps you create predictable habits so you know what to focus on each day. A routine also reduces the stress of making decisions because the plan is already in place. With a routine, your study time becomes more consistent and easier to maintain. Why Are Study Routines Important? Study routines matter because they make school feel more manageable day to day. Instead of guessing what to work on, you have a plan that supports your goals and reduces some of the chaos around assignments and exams. Here are a few reasons why study routines are important: They help you stay focused - A consistent routine teaches your brain when it is time to study, so it becomes easier to get into the right mindset. Over time, you spend less energy fighting distractions and more time actually learning. They make you feel less overwhelmed - When you already know what you will work on and when, there is less pressure and panic. You spread the workload across the week instead of trying to handle everything at once. They help you remember more - Regular review sessions help information stick, which is important for quizzes, exams, and future classes. You give yourself more chances to revisit material before you forget it. They help you balance school and life - A routine helps you fit studying around jobs, activities, and personal time. They are great productivity hacks that help you balance time better. When you treat studying as a habit instead of something you only do before a test , school feels more predictable and less stressful. A solid routine gives you a structure you can adjust as your schedule and classes change. What Goes Into an Effective Study Routine? A strong study routine is built on habits and tools that help you stay organized and focused. The goal is to make your study time predictable, manageable, and easier to maintain. Here's what is typically included in an effective study routine: Time management - Setting specific study blocks and sticking to them helps you stay consistent and avoid rushing through work. Study methods - Using approaches like active recall, note taking, and practice questions makes each session more effective. Weekly planning - Looking ahead at upcoming assignments and exams helps you spread the work out instead of cramming. Breaks and pacing - Short breaks help you reset and stay focused for longer periods of time. A steady study space - Having a reliable place to study reduces distractions and helps you settle in quicker. Progress tracking - Paying attention to what works and what doesn’t allows you to adjust your routine over time. Tools, apps, and resources - Having a good tech stack can take a study routine from good to great. When you combine these pieces with study hacks , studying becomes easier to manage and more aligned with your goals. Want to boost your study game with AI? How to Develop a Consistent Study Routine Building a consistent study routine starts with understanding your schedule and choosing habits you can maintain. Here's how to develop a consistent study routine: 1. Look at your weekly schedule Take a close look at your classes, work hours, and personal commitments. This helps you understand how much time you actually have available for studying. When you see your week clearly, it becomes easier to find realistic study blocks. 2. Decide how many study sessions you need Think about the number of classes you have and how demanding they are. Choose a reasonable number of sessions that you can commit to each week. Keep the plan realistic so that it's easier to stay consistent. The simpler and more realistic it is, the easier it is to follow. 3. Pick study methods that match your goals Different classes may require reading, problem solving, or memorization, so choose methods that support the type of learning you need. Active recall, note taking, rote memorization , and practice questions can all help you stay engaged. Matching the method to the material makes your time more productive. 4. Create a simple plan for each session Plan what you want to cover before you start studying. A short outline helps you avoid wasting time deciding what to do next. This small step keeps each session focused and organized. 5. Use tools or apps that support your routine Study apps can help you stay organized, set reminders, or turn material into notes or flashcards. They make it easier to keep track of your tasks and stay consistent throughout the week. Adding the right apps to your routine can remove guesswork and help you focus on the actual studying. Check out our advice below on how to use study apps in your daily routine . 6. Include breaks to stay energized Short breaks help prevent mental fatigue and make longer study sessions feel easier. Breaks give you a moment to reset so you can return to the material with better focus. They are an important part of staying consistent over time. 7. Adjust your routine as needed Check in with yourself each week to see what is working and what feels difficult. Small adjustments can make your routine easier to follow. This structure gives you a routine that is repeatable and realistic. You can adjust the days and tasks based on your classes, but the flow stays the same: plan, study, review, and refine. FAQ What Methods Should I Use in My Study Routine? Different methods help you learn in different ways, so using a mix can make your study routine more effective. Choosing the right approach depends on your classes and how you prefer to learn. Here are a few of the most popular and effective study methods to use in your study routine: SQ3R - Using the Survey, Question, Read, Recite, Review process helps you stay active while reading. It breaks long chapters into steps that improve comprehension and retention. Note taking - Writing or rewriting notes helps you organize information in a way that makes sense to you. This is especially useful when working through lectures or assigned readings. Summarizing - Turning chapters or lectures into short summaries helps you identify the main ideas. It also makes future review sessions faster and more focused. Active recall - Asking yourself questions or quizzing yourself helps you check what you truly understand. This method strengthens memory and prepares you for exams . Spaced repetition - Reviewing material over several days helps information stick for the long term. Flashcards or apps make this method easier to follow. Rote memorization - Repeating facts or definitions helps you store information that must be recalled exactly. This works well for vocabulary, formulas, and essential terms. Teaching the material - Explaining a concept out loud shows whether you understand it clearly. It also reinforces what you already know. Practice problems - Solving problems or completing exercises gives you hands-on experience with the material. This is helpful in math, science, and subjects that rely on step-by-step processes. Using a blend of these methods helps you stay engaged and learn more effectively. You can rotate between them based on what each class requires and what feels most helpful. body_text: – Financing includes leading U.S. biotechnology institutional investors and mutual funds – LOS ANGELES, CA, Dec. 09, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Immix Biopharma, Inc. (“ImmixBio”, “Company”, “We” or “Us” or “IMMX”), a global leader in relapsed/refractory AL Amyloidosis, today announced the closing of its previously announced underwritten registered offering of 19,117,646 shares of its common stock at a price to the public of $5.10 per share, and to certain investors in lieu of common stock, pre-funded warrants to purchase 490,196 shares of common stock at a price to the public of $5.09 per pre-funded warrant, which represents the per share public offering price for the common stock, less the $0.01 per share exercise price for each such pre-funded warrant. The net proceeds to Immix from the offering, after deducting the underwriting discounts, commissions and other offering expenses, were approximately $93.7 million. The financing includes leading U.S. biotechnology institutional investors and mutual funds. Morgan Stanley acted as the sole book-running manager for the offering. Citizens Capital Markets and Mizuho acted as co-managers for the offering. The securities in the registered offering were offered and sold pursuant to a “shelf” registration statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-269100), including a base prospectus, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on January 3, 2023, and declared effective on January 11, 2023. A prospectus supplement and accompanying prospectus describing the terms of the registered offering was filed with the SEC and is available on its website at www.sec.gov . Copies of the prospectus supplement and the accompanying prospectus relating to the offering may also be obtained from: Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, attention: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, New York 10014, by phone: 1-866-718-1649 or by email: prospectus@morganstanley.com. This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy any of the securities described herein, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction. About Immix Biopharma, Inc. Immix Biopharma, Inc. (ImmixBio) (Nasdaq: IMMX) is a global leader in relapsed/refractory AL Amyloidosis. AL Amyloidosis is a devastating disease where the immune system, that’s supposed to protect, instead produces toxic light chains, clogging up the heart, kidney and liver, causing organ failure and death. Our lead candidate is sterically-optimized BCMA-targeted chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy NXC-201 with a “digital filter” that is designed to filter out non-specific activation. NXC-201 teaches the immune system to recognize and eliminate the source of the toxic light chains. NXC-201 is being evaluated in the U.S. multi-center study for relapsed/refractory AL Amyloidosis NEXICART-2 (NCT06097832), with a registrational design. NXC-201 has been awarded Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) by the US FDA and Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) by FDA and in the EU by the EMA. title: How to Identify the Next Big Consumer Trend Before It Goes Mainstream
summary: Learn how to spot emerging consumer trends early using search data, social signals and AI-powered forecasting to stay ahead of the competition.
body_text: Spot the Next Big Consumer Trend Before Your Competitors Do Consumer trends move quickly. What gains traction today can plateau within months. If a trend is already peaking by the time you act, the window for differentiation may have closed. Late entry does more than impact brand perception. It can result in misallocated inventory, delayed product development, and investment in categories where demand is already stabilizing. Trend forecasting is no longer optional for brands operating in fast-moving categories. Traditional marketing instincts and retrospective reporting often identify trends after they have scaled. By then, brands are reacting rather than shaping the market. Consider the rise of “ booty beauty .” As consumer interest expanded beyond facial skincare to body-specific treatments, early niche brands captured demand quickly. Larger players eventually entered the space, but those that identified the signal early established stronger positioning and category authority. The goal is not to chase every viral moment. It is to identify credible signals early enough to inform product development, messaging, and investment decisions. Why Traditional Market Research Misses Emerging Trends Traditional market research was designed for long-term stability, not market velocity. Surveys, focus groups, and quarterly reports offer valuable strategic context, but they reflect behavior that has already occurred. By the time insights are compiled and distributed, consumer interest may have shifted. Emerging trend identification requires analyzing behavioral signals as they develop. Instead of relying solely on what consumers say in structured environments, brands benefit from observing what people are actively searching for and engaging with across digital platforms. Search and social data provide a current view of curiosity and intent, allowing brands to shorten the feedback loop and make more forward-looking decisions. Search Data Reveals What Consumers Want Before They Buy Search behavior is one of the clearest indicators of consumer intent. Before purchasing, consumers research ingredients, routines, claims, and comparisons. Analyzing search volume alongside trajectory patterns enables brands to identify demand during its growth phase rather than after it matures. Search data also surfaces the language consumers use to describe their needs. That phrasing often reveals emerging concerns, shifting priorities, and gaps in the market. These insights can inform product development, naming strategy, and messaging. Spate analyzes billions of Google search signals across beauty, wellness, food, and CPG categories to identify sustained momentum and evaluate predictive trajectory, helping brands prioritize opportunities with measurable demand. Social Signals That Indicate a Trend Is About to Explode Social platforms frequently surface early experimentation and cultural adoption. Rising hashtag usage, repeated creator engagement, and steady increases in content production can signal growing interest. However, visibility alone is not validation. A single viral post may generate significant attention without translating into lasting demand. More durable opportunities tend to show sustained engagement over time and participation across multiple creator tiers. When increasing social conversation aligns with upward search patterns, confidence in the trend’s longevity strengthens. The key is distinguishing between short-lived amplification and measurable trajectory. The Difference Between Microtrends and Long-Term Shifts Not every upward signal represents a structural shift. Microtrends often spike quickly within niche communities before declining just as rapidly. Long-term trends, by contrast, demonstrate steady growth across broader audiences and sustained timeframes. Evaluating growth velocity over multiple months, breadth of adoption, and cross-platform consistency helps differentiate between the two. Trends that align with broader category or cultural movements are more likely to endure than isolated moments of attention. Consistent engagement across creators, categories, and search behavior indicates deeper consumer interest, while sharp spikes without continued follow-through often signal temporary fascination. Strategic investment should focus on trends that demonstrate staying power rather than volatility. Platform Specific Behaviors and Cross Channel Validation Trends rarely emerge evenly across the digital ecosystem. Many begin on a single platform and expand outward as adoption widens. Observing interest across both search and social platforms strengthens confidence that a trend reflects broader consumer demand rather than platform-specific behavior. Adoption patterns may also vary by audience segment and platform norms. A trend can gain early traction within creator communities before becoming more visible in search data as interest broadens. Monitoring how signals transition across platforms provides insight into how demand matures and where messaging or product development may need to evolve. Using AI and Machine Intelligence to Identify Consumer Trends Trend analysis requires processing large-scale datasets across categories, platforms, and timeframes. Manual approaches cannot efficiently surface patterns at this scale. AI and machine learning enable structured analysis of search and social behavior, identifying emerging signals, clustering related themes, and evaluating growth patterns. Spate applies AI-driven analysis to assess whether momentum reflects sustained consumer interest or short-term volatility. Predictive modeling supports forward-looking planning across product development, marketing, and strategic investment, allowing teams to prioritize initiatives with greater confidence. Reading the Signals: Search Volume Growth and Trajectory Analysis When assessing potential trends, trajectory carries more weight than isolated spikes. Sustained upward movement over multiple months signals stronger demand than brief peaks. Year-over-year comparisons provide helpful context, but consistency and continued forward momentum are more reliable indicators of durability. Seasonality patterns also matter. Recurring increases in interest can represent dependable innovation opportunities, while narrow spikes often indicate short-lived attention. Emerging trends typically broaden over time, expanding across related categories and audiences. Microtrends tend to remain concentrated and volatile. ‍ Turn Consumer Trend Insights Into Actionable Strategy Identifying signals is only valuable if they inform action. The advantage lies in translating behavioral data into product, marketing, and positioning decisions grounded in measurable demand. Spate provides a structured data foundation for innovation and competitive strategy by analyzing large-scale search and social behavior. With greater visibility into developing interest patterns, brands can prioritize pipelines, refine messaging, and evaluate whitespace opportunities earlier in the cycle. Instead of reacting to what has already scaled, teams can align strategy with observable shifts in consumer demand and move with greater precision. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) How early can you predict consumer trends before they go mainstream? The timing varies by category and platform, but consistent monitoring of search and social growth patterns can surface emerging shifts months before they reach peak visibility. The key is identifying sustained upward momentum rather than reacting to sudden spikes. When growth demonstrates consistency across multiple signals, brands gain a meaningful head start in product development and positioning. What data sources are most reliable for spotting emerging trends? Search behavior and social engagement are two of the strongest indicators of developing demand. Search data reveals active intent and problem-solving behavior, while social data highlights experimentation and cultural adoption. When signals align across both channels, confidence in a trend’s potential increases. Cross-channel analysis provides a more complete view than relying on a single source How do you distinguish between a fad and a lasting trend? Fads typically appear as sharp increases in attention followed by rapid decline, often driven by a single viral moment. Lasting trends show steadier growth across longer timeframes and broader audiences. Evaluating trajectory, consistency, and cross-platform adoption helps determine whether interest reflects temporary visibility or a deeper shift in consumer priorities. What industries benefit most from consumer trend forecasting? Any industry that operates in competitive, innovation-driven environments benefits from early visibility into consumer demand. This is particularly true for beauty, wellness, food, and CPG categories, where product cycles move quickly and consumer preferences evolve rapidly. In these spaces, identifying signals earlier can directly influence speed to market and category positioning. How often should brands monitor consumer trends and search data? Ongoing monitoring is critical in fast-moving markets. Reviewing behavioral data on a consistent cadence, such as biweekly or monthly, allows brands to track trajectory changes and emerging patterns before they mature. Regular evaluation supports more proactive decision-making and reduces reliance on outdated or retrospective insights. ‍

title: The Week in Web Development: Coursera-Udemy Merger, AI-Powered Formal Verification, and Mozilla's Leadership Change
summary: From the Coursera-Udemy merger to AI-powered formal verification and Mozilla's leadership transition, this week's developments reveal important trends in web development, developer education, and the future of building software.
body_text: This week brought major shifts in the developer landscape: a $1.2 billion education platform merger, breakthrough thinking on AI-assisted formal verification, and significant leadership changes at Mozilla. Here's what these developments mean for developers and the future of web development. Coursera and Udemy Join Forces Coursera announced they're combining with Udemy in a $1.2 billion deal that creates a unified platform for professional skills development. The merger combines Coursera's university partnerships with Udemy's extensive marketplace of technical courses. For developers, this consolidation matters because: Unified Learning Paths : Instead of navigating two separate platforms, developers can access both structured academic programs and practical, hands-on courses in one place. This makes it easier to build comprehensive skill sets that combine theoretical foundations with real-world application. AI-Era Skills Focus : The combined platform emphasizes "skills for the AI era" - exactly what developers need as AI capabilities become standard expectations in web development. Courses on prompt engineering, AI integration, and building AI-powered applications will likely see expanded coverage. Corporate Training Impact : Many development teams use these platforms for professional development. A merged platform could streamline corporate learning programs, making it easier for organizations to provide comprehensive training. The Hacker News discussion reveals mixed reactions from the developer community, with some concerned about reduced competition while others see potential benefits from unified content catalogs. AI Making Formal Verification Accessible Martin Kleppmann's article on how AI will make formal verification go mainstream presents a compelling vision for how large language models could democratize software correctness. What is Formal Verification? Formal verification mathematically proves that software behaves correctly - no bugs, no edge cases, no "it works on my machine" surprises. Traditionally, this required specialized expertise in formal methods and tools like TLA+, making it accessible only to experts and critical systems. How AI Changes the Game Kleppmann argues that AI assistants can: Translate natural language to formal specifications : Developers describe what their code should do in plain language, and AI generates the formal specification. Generate proofs automatically : Instead of manually constructing complex proofs, AI can explore the proof space and find valid proofs of correctness. Explain verification failures : When proofs fail, AI can explain why in understandable terms and suggest fixes. Iterate on specifications : AI can help refine specifications based on counterexamples and edge cases it discovers. The extensive Hacker News discussion reveals both excitement and skepticism. Experienced developers note that formal verification's real challenge isn't proving code correct - it's knowing what "correct" means in the first place. Implications for Web Development For web developers, AI-assisted formal verification could mean: More reliable APIs : Critical business logic could be formally verified, eliminating entire classes of bugs. Better security : Security properties could be proven rather than tested, preventing vulnerabilities. Clearer specifications : The process of creating formal specs improves understanding of requirements. Faster iteration : Catching logic errors before writing code saves debugging time. As one commenter noted, "The bottleneck isn't proving things - it's figuring out what to prove." AI that helps developers articulate and refine their specifications could be more valuable than AI that generates proofs. Mozilla's New Direction Under New Leadership Mozilla appointed Anthony Enzor-Demeo as their new CEO , marking a significant leadership transition for the organization behind Firefox and numerous web standards. The timing is notable: Mozilla faces challenges maintaining Firefox's relevance while also pursuing new revenue streams through services and partnerships. The Hacker News discussion reflects community concerns about Mozilla's direction. Why This Matters to Developers Mozilla's role extends beyond Firefox: Web Standards Leadership : Mozilla actively shapes web standards through W3C participation and Firefox implementation. Strong Mozilla leadership matters for keeping the web open and interoperable. Developer Tools : Firefox DevTools remain popular among developers for CSS debugging, accessibility testing, and performance analysis. Continued investment in these tools depends on Mozilla's strategic direction. Privacy Advocacy : Mozilla's advocacy for user privacy influences browser features, web standards, and industry practices. This advocacy becomes more important as AI features collect more user data. Open Source Ecosystem : Mozilla supports numerous open source projects beyond Firefox, including Rust (though now independent), MDN Web Docs, and various web technologies. A follow-up article asking "Is Mozilla trying hard to kill itself?" generated significant discussion about Mozilla's strategy and whether recent decisions serve developers' interests. Related Developments Worth Watching GitHub Actions Pricing Changes GitHub announced pricing changes for GitHub Actions that affect how teams budget for CI/CD. Starting March 2026, self-hosted runners will no longer be free, prompting many teams to reevaluate their automation strategies. The active discussion shows developers weighing alternatives like GitLab CI, CircleCI, and Jenkins. Patches are available in React 19.0.1+ and Next.js 15.0.5+. For Cosmic users, all new Next.js deployments through our platform automatically use the patched versions. Developer Education Evolves The Coursera-Udemy merger reflects how developer learning is shifting toward practical, skills-based training that combines theory with hands-on practice. As AI capabilities expand, developers need to stay current with new tools and patterns. 3. Tools Must Justify Complexity GitHub's pricing changes and Mozilla's direction show that developers increasingly question whether tools justify their complexity and cost. Platforms that provide value without operational overhead will gain adoption. 4. Security and Correctness Matter More With formal verification becoming more accessible and security vulnerabilities having broader impact, developers face increasing pressure to build correct, secure software from the start.
